description: tonyd2wild's two-Spark vLLM TP2 SPEED profile for NVIDIA's own nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 checkpoint, used byte for byte (124 GB). The n-gram table stays in unified memory (each Spark holds its half, stock loader), decode runs as CUDA graphs with torch.compile off, MTP 3, six sequences, 4,096-token prefill chunks, FP8 KV, memory utilization 0.70 and 262,144 context (upstream defaults; upstream's CONTEXT profile keeps the table on disk and is one option). The adapter bakes upstream's patch files and vLLM overlays into the image at upstream's exact vLLM commit 8a728663 (PR #55375 fused PLE state-index fix, PR #54846 FP8/NVFP4 KV on the QSA path, two ModelOpt MTP-loading fixes). Upstream launches the ranks with vLLM's multiprocess backend (--nnodes, --node-rank, --headless), the same as the Controller does, so the launch shape is unchanged. Image note: upstream ran the vllm/vllm-openai nightly-8a728663 tag, which is no longer on Docker Hub; the same commit survives only as the cu129-nightly-8a728663 build, pinned here by digest (CUDA 12.9 runtime instead of upstream's CUDA 13), so a Spark start is unverified. Licences (information only): repository Apache-2.0; vLLM Apache-2.0; checkpoint under the NVIDIA Open Model License and the Qwen licence of the base model. Upstream throughput figures are claims until measured here; Vonk physical acceptance is pending. Alternative from another creator: MiaAI-Lab's dual kit (see the Mia recipe). GB10 memory correction: Per-node peak budgets utilization × 130,663,231,488-byte unified memory plus at least 8 GB for CUDA context/graphs, FlashInfer workspace, auxiliary heads and CPU/mmap buffers; 8 GB reserve, with a separate 6 GB OS floor. This is a conservative budget, not a measured footprint.
title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next NVFP4 vLLM two Sparks (tonyd2wild)
